obligations.statement: The product must include a foot pedal for a workbench.
derivation_premises: A product that does not include a foot pedal cannot satisfy the requirement.

obligations.statement: A signal must be sent when the pedal is pressed.
derivation_premises: A signal can only be sent if physical motion or contact is generated by pressing.

obligations.statement: The pedal must return to its resting position on its own when the foot is removed.
derivation_premises: Without a restoring mechanism, the pedal would remain displaced after release.

obligations.statement: The pedal must not move when brushed sideways.
derivation_premises: A pedal that is free to move in the sideways direction will move when brushed.

obligations.statement: The pedal must be reachable by the user's foot.
derivation_premises: The user must be able to reach the pedal to operate it.

obligations.statement: The pedal must be able to be pressed by the user.
derivation_premises: Pressing requires an accessible surface that can be displaced.

obligations.statement: The pedal must be stable under its own weight when at rest.
derivation_premises: A pedal that is not stable would move unintentionally.

obligations.statement: The product must be able to transmit the pressing force to a signal generation mechanism.
derivation_premises: Without load transmission, the pressing force cannot trigger a signal.

obligations.statement: The pedal must not move when brushed sideways.
derivation_premises: If the pedal has a degree of freedom in the sideways direction, it will move.

obligations.statement: The pedal must not trigger a signal when brushed sideways.
derivation_premises: If the pedal moves sideways enough, it could inadvertently trigger the signal.

obligations.statement: The pedal must return to its resting position after each release.
derivation_premises: Repeated operation requires consistent return to rest.

candidates.summary: A pedal that uses a revolute pair for rotation, a spring for return, and a limit stop for sideways blocking.

evidence_route_verdict.note: A revolute pair allows rotation but not translation, so sideways brush would not cause motion if the pivot is aligned vertically.

candidates.summary: A pedal that uses a prismatic pair for vertical translation, a spring for return, and a guide that resists sideways motion.

evidence_route_verdict.note: A prismatic pair with a vertical axis would constrain sideways motion.

candidates.summary: A pedal that uses a compliant flexure for vertical deflection and return, with geometry that resists sideways motion.

evidence_route_verdict.note: A flexure can be designed to be compliant in one direction and stiff in another.

predicates: The pedal must have a revolute joint allowing rotation about a horizontal axis.
A return spring must be present to restore the pedal to its resting position.
A hard stop must prevent sideways motion.
The pedal must have a prismatic joint allowing vertical translation.
A return spring must be present to restore the pedal to its resting position.
The prismatic guide must constrain sideways motion.
The pedal must have a compliant flexure allowing vertical deflection.
The flexure must provide a restoring force.
The flexure must be stiff in the sideways direction.

unresolved.decision: Whether the pedal must not move at all when brushed sideways or may move but not trigger a signal.
unresolved.why_open: The requirement is ambiguous and the candidates differ in how they address it.

assumptions.statement: The signal is intended to control the machine.
assumptions.why: The request says pressing sends a signal to the machine, implying control.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: a clarification that the signal is purely informational or for other purposes.

assumptions.statement: The pedal is normally in a resting position.
assumptions.why: The request mentions returning to its resting position, implying such a position exists.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: a statement that the pedal does not have a defined resting position.
